fullPassage:
What does it mean to be brave? There is no single definition, but everyone is brave in their own way. Here are three young people sharing their bravest moments in life.

Jason
One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I immediately called 911 and explained the situation. The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived. I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right. A few minutes later, the paramedics rushed in and took over the situation. Luckily, the clerk regained consciousness. After putting the clerk in the ambulance, the paramedics said "Thank you for being brave. You did a wonderful job." It felt great to help save someone's life!

Olivia
I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and awards from races I had competed in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end. I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track. At first, I didn't think much of the injury. I thought I would get better soon. But the test results from the hospital were not hopeful. The doctors said my knee injury would prevent me from running again.

Every night, I had flashbacks of my injury. I could not watch sports anymore because it was just too painful. So I shut out everything related to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called sports medicine. It deals with the treatment and prevention of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head. This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears. So I made up my mind and applied to this major. Today, thanks to my brave decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines instead of on the playing field.

Yuna
Ever since I was young, I have admired great public speakers. I hoped to inspire and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get scared. I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it. That's why I never entered the annual speech contest at my school. I really wanted to, but I just didn't have enough courage. Last year, however, was my final chance before graduating from high school. When I saw the poster on the class board, my mind began to fill with thoughts of the school speech contest. I heard a voice growing louder in my head, saying "Go for it!" I decided to sign up for the contest. To make a long story short, I did it. I delivered my speech to the entire school. How did I do? Honestly, I don't remember much from the contest because I was so nervous. But my act of courage taught me a valuable lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to.

questions.passage: One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was (A)[wrong / right]. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk (B)[lying / standing] on the floor. I (C)[immediately / reluctantly] called 911 and explained the situation.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 어느 날 저녁, 나는 군것질거리를 사려고 편의점에 갔다. 계산대에 아무도 없어서 점원이 뒤쪽에서 일하고 있다고 생각했다. 전화가 울리기 시작했는데 아무도 전화를 받으러 오지 않았다. 나는 뭔가 잘못되었다고 느꼈다. 계산대 너머를 보니 점원이 바닥에 누워 있는 것이 보였다. 나는 즉시 911에 전화를 걸어 상황을 설명했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① wrong — lying — immediately
❌ ② right — lying — immediately
❌ ③ wrong — standing — immediately
❌ ④ wrong — lying — reluctantly
✅ (A) wrong: 전화에 아무도 안 오는 비정상적 상황이므로 '잘못된'이 적절. right(옳은)은 문맥과 반대. ✅ (B) lying: 바닥에 '누워' 있는 것이므로 lying이 적절. standing(서 있는)은 on the floor와 어울리지 않음. ✅ (C) immediately: 위급 상황에서 '즉시' 전화한 것. reluctantly(마지못해)는 적극적 구조 행동과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: wrong: 잘못된 (↔ right), lying: 누워 있는 (lie–lay–lain), immediately: 즉시 (= at once, right away)

questions.passage: Every night, I had (A)[flashbacks / expectations] of my injury. I could not watch sports anymore because it was just too painful. So I shut out everything (B)[related / compared] to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my (C)[ordinary / extraordinary] high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called sports medicine.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 매일 밤 나는 부상에 대한 기억이 떠올랐다. 너무 괴로워서 더 이상 스포츠 경기를 볼 수 없었다. 그래서 내 인생에서 스포츠와 관련된 모든 것을 차단했다. 2년이 흘렀고 나는 운동을 하지 않는 평범한 고등학교 생활에 익숙해지려고 여전히 노력 중이었다. 그러던 어느 날, 스포츠 의학이라는 흥미로운 대학 전공을 우연히 알게 되었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① flashbacks — compared — ordinary
❌ ② expectations — related — ordinary
❌ ③ flashbacks — related — extraordinary
✅ ④ flashbacks — related — ordinary
✅ (A) flashbacks: 부상의 고통스러운 '회상/플래시백'. expectations(기대)는 부정적 맥락에 부적절. ✅ (B) related: 'related to'는 '~와 관련된'. compared to(~와 비교하면)는 shut out과 어울리지 않음. ✅ (C) ordinary: 스포츠 없는 '평범한' 생활. extraordinary(비범한)는 반대 의미.
det.tip: flashback: 과거 기억의 재현, shut out: 차단하다, get used to: ~에 익숙해지다, ordinary ↔ extraordinary

questions.passage: Ever since I was young, I have (A)[admired / despised] great public speakers. I hoped to (B)[inspire / discourage] and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get scared. I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me (C)[behind / beyond] the stage rather than on it.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 어릴 때부터 나는 뛰어난 대중 연설가들을 동경해 왔다. 언젠가는 그들처럼 청중을 고무하고 감동을 주기를 바랐다. 하지만 사람들 앞에서 말할 기회가 있을 때마다 겁에 질리곤 했다. 웃음거리가 되고 싶지 않았다. 이 두려움 때문에 무대 위가 아닌 무대 뒤에 있게 되었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① admired — inspire — beyond
✅ ② admired — inspire — behind
❌ ③ despised — inspire — behind
❌ ④ admired — discourage — behind
✅ (A) admired: 연설가를 '동경'했다는 긍정 맥락. despised(경멸했다)는 반대. ✅ (B) inspire: 청중을 '고무하다'. discourage(낙담시키다)는 반대. ✅ (C) behind: 무대 '뒤에' 숨었다는 맥락. beyond(너머에)는 rather than on it과 대비 불가. ❌ ①은 beyond 오답, ③은 despised 오답, ④는 discourage 오답.
det.tip: admire: 동경하다 (= look up to ↔ despise), inspire: 고무하다 (↔ discourage), behind the stage: 무대 뒤에

questions.passage: The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived. I was ①<u>scared</u>, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to ②<u>push</u> down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right. A few minutes later, the paramedics rushed in and took over the situation. ③<u>Unfortunately</u>, the clerk regained ④<u>consciousness</u>.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 교환원은 구급대원이 도착할 때까지 점원에게 심폐소생술을 해 달라고 요청했다. 나는 ①겁이 났지만 학교에서 심폐소생술을 배운 기억이 났다. 제대로 하고 있기를 바라며 그의 가슴을 ②압박하기 시작했다. 몇 분 후 구급대원이 들어와 상황을 넘겨받았다. ③불행히도(→다행히도) 점원은 ④의식을 되찾았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① scared: 위급 상황에서 '겁나다'는 자연스러움. ✅ ② push: CPR에서 가슴을 '압박하다'. ❌ ③ Unfortunately(불행히도): 원문은 Luckily(다행히도). 점원이 의식을 되찾은 것은 다행스러운 일이므로 Unfortunately는 문맥상 부적절. ✅ ④ consciousness: '의식'을 되찾다는 자연스러움.
det.tip: luckily(다행히도) ↔ unfortunately(불행히도), regain consciousness: 의식을 되찾다

questions.passage: I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and ①<u>penalties</u> from races I had competed in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a ②<u>sudden</u> end. I was about to take the ③<u>lead</u> in the race when I suddenly felt a ④<u>pain</u> in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 나는 올림픽 육상 선수가 되는 것이 꿈이었다. 내 방은 출전했던 경기에서 획득한 메달과 ①벌칙들(→상들)로 가득 차 있었다. 하지만 전국 100미터 선수권 대회 도중에 올림픽에 대한 내 꿈은 ②갑작스럽게 끝났다. 경기에서 ③선두를 잡으려던 순간 갑자기 무릎에서 ④통증이 느껴졌다. 땅에 쓰러졌고 트랙 밖으로 옮겨져야 했다.
det.analysis: ❌ ① penalties(벌칙): 원문은 awards(상). 메달(medals)과 함께 나열되므로 '상'이 적절. penalties는 부정적 의미로 문맥상 부적절. ✅ ② sudden: '갑작스러운' 끝. ✅ ③ lead: '선두'를 잡으려 하다(take the lead). ✅ ④ pain: 무릎의 '통증'.
det.tip: awards: 상, 수상 (↔ penalties: 벌칙, 벌금), take the lead: 선두를 잡다, come to an end: 끝나다

questions.passage: When I saw the poster on the class board, my mind began to fill with thoughts of the school speech contest. I heard a voice growing louder in my head, saying 'Go for it!' I decided to ①<u>sign up</u> for the contest. To make a long story short, I did it. I ②<u>delivered</u> my speech to the entire school. But my act of ③<u>courage</u> taught me a ④<u>worthless</u> lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 학급 게시판에서 포스터를 보았을 때, 내 마음은 교내 웅변대회에 대한 생각으로 가득 차기 시작했다. '한번 해 봐!'라고 말하는 목소리가 머릿속에서 점점 크게 들렸다. 나는 대회에 ①참가 신청을 하기로 결심했다. 간단히 말하면, 내가 해냈다. 전교생 앞에서 ②연설했다. 하지만 나의 ③용기 있는 행동은 내게 ④무가치한(→값진) 교훈을 주었다: 마음먹으면 무엇이든 할 수 있다는 것.
det.analysis: ✅ ① sign up: 대회에 '참가 신청하다'. ✅ ② delivered: 연설을 '전달하다'. ✅ ③ courage: '용기' 있는 행동. ❌ ④ worthless(무가치한): 원문은 valuable(값진). '마음먹으면 무엇이든 할 수 있다'는 긍정적 교훈이므로 worthless는 문맥상 부적절.
det.tip: valuable(값진) ↔ worthless(무가치한), sign up for: ~에 참가 신청하다, deliver a speech: 연설하다, put one's mind to: 마음먹고 하다

det.tip: run의 다의어: 달리다(sprint), 운영하다(operate/manage), 작동하다(function), 흐르다(flow)

det.analysis: ✅ ③ consciousness: '의식'으로 영영 풀이와 정확히 일치. ❌ ① convenience(편의): 편리함. ❌ ② ambulance(구급차): 의료 차량. ❌ ④ conference(회의): 모임.
det.tip: consciousness: 의식 (conscious: 의식이 있는 ↔ unconscious: 의식이 없는), regain consciousness: 의식을 되찾다

questions.passage: I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I called 911 and __________ (explain) the situation.
questions.stem: 위 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 뭔가 잘못되었다고 느꼈다. 계산대 너머를 보니 바닥에 점원이 쓰러져 있었다. 나는 911에 전화를 걸어 상황을 설명했다.
det.analysis: called와 병렬 구조로 과거형 explained가 적절. 'called 911 and explained'에서 and로 연결된 두 동사는 같은 시제(과거형).
det.tip: explain → explained (과거형), 병렬 구조: A and B에서 A와 B는 같은 형태

questions.passage: Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called sports medicine. It deals with the treatment and __________ (prevent) of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head.
questions.stem: 위 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 스포츠 의학이라는 흥미로운 대학 전공을 우연히 알게 되었다. 그것은 스포츠 부상의 치료와 예방에 대해 다루었다.
det.analysis: treatment and __________ 구조에서 and 앞의 treatment가 명사이므로 빈칸에도 명사가 와야 한다. prevent(동사) → prevention(명사).
det.tip: prevent(v.) → prevention(n.): 예방. 병렬 구조에서 and 앞뒤는 같은 품사.

questions.passage:
What does it mean to be brave? There is no single definition, but everyone is brave in their own way. Here are three young people sharing their bravest moments in life.

Jason
One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I immediately called 911 and explained the situation. The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived. I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right. A few minutes later, the paramedics rushed in and took over the situation. Luckily, the clerk regained consciousness. After putting the clerk in the ambulance, the paramedics said "Thank you for being brave. You did a wonderful job." It felt great to help save someone's life!

Olivia
I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and awards from races I had competed in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end. I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track. At first, I didn't think much of the injury. I thought I would get better soon. But the test results from the hospital were not hopeful. The doctors said my knee injury would prevent me from running again.

Every night, I had flashbacks of my injury. I could not watch sports anymore because it was just too painful. So I shut out everything related to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called sports medicine. It deals with the treatment and prevention of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head. This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears. So I made up my mind and applied to this major. Today, thanks to my brave decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines instead of on the playing field.

Yuna
Ever since I was young, I have admired great public speakers. I hoped to inspire and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get scared. I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it. That's why I never entered the annual speech contest at my school. I really wanted to, but I just didn't have enough courage. Last year, however, was my final chance before graduating from high school. When I saw the poster on the class board, my mind began to fill with thoughts of the school speech contest. I heard a voice growing louder in my head, saying "Go for it!" I decided to ____ the contest. To make a long story short, I did it. I delivered my speech to the entire school. How did I do? Honestly, I don't remember much from the contest because I was so nervous. But my act of courage taught me a valuable lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정말 해 보고는 싶었지만, 단지 용기가 부족했다. 하지만 지난해는 고등학교를 졸업하기 전 마지막 기회였다. 학급 게시판에서 포스터를 보았을 때, 내 마음은 교내 웅변대회에 대한 생각으로 가득 차기 시작했다. '한번 해 봐!'라는 목소리가 머릿속에서 점점 크게 들렸다. 나는 대회에 참가 신청하기로 결심했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② sign up for: 목소리가 'Go for it!'이라고 격려하고 마지막 기회라는 맥락에서 대회에 '참가 신청하다'가 적절. ❌ ① give up on(포기하다): 격려 맥락과 반대. ❌ ③ drop out of(중도 탈퇴하다): 아직 참가 전이므로 부적절. ❌ ④ complain about(불평하다): 문맥 부적절.
det.tip: sign up for: ~에 참가 신청하다 (= register for, enroll in), go for it: 한번 해 봐!

questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그러던 어느 날, 스포츠 의학이라는 흥미로운 대학 전공을 알게 되었다. 머릿속에 번뜩 좋은 생각이 떠올랐다. 이것은 나의 고민과 두려움에서 도망치는 것을 멈출 기회였다. 그래서 마음을 먹고 이 전공에 지원했다. 용기 있는 결정 덕분에 경기장 대신 사이드라인의 주인공이 되기 위해 공부하고 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① made up my mind: '결심하다'로 brave decision과 연결되며 applied(지원했다)로 이어지는 맥락에 적절. ❌ ② changed the subject(화제를 바꾸다): 진로 결정과 무관. ❌ ③ lost my temper(화를 내다): 용기 있는 결정과 무관. ❌ ④ broke the ice(어색한 분위기를 깨다): 진로 결정 맥락과 무관.
det.tip: make up one's mind: 결심하다 (= decide, determine), apply to: ~에 지원하다, a light bulb went on: 좋은 생각이 떠오르다
